cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to give you an example of a one-way ANOVA.
cues.zh: 講師：這支影片要舉一個單因子 ANOVA 的例子。

cues.en: This will give you a little bit more experience interpreting ANOVA results and we can talk a bit more about the ANOVA table and so on.
cues.zh: 讓你累積更多解讀 ANOVA 結果的經驗，也能多談一些 ANOVA 表等等。

cues.en: Okay, so, let's say we are interested in doing some scientific research.
cues.zh: 假設我們想進行科學研究。

cues.en: We want to know whether people are happier after watching specific types of movies, so different genres of movies.
cues.zh: 想知道人們觀看特定類型，也就是不同類型的電影之後，是否更快樂。

cues.en: So we set up an experiment.
cues.zh: 所以設計一個實驗。

cues.en: We have our independent variables and dependent variables.
cues.zh: 有自變數與依變數。

cues.en: The independent variable is movie genre.
cues.zh: 自變數是電影類型。

cues.en: So it's just one factor.
cues.zh: 只有一個因子。

cues.en: And we have four levels, or four groups, of this factor.
cues.zh: 因子有四個水準，或四個群組。

cues.en: Horror movies, romcom, which as I recently learned stands for romantic comedy, documentaries, and sci-fi flicks.
cues.zh: 恐怖片、romcom，我最近才知道是浪漫喜劇的縮寫、紀錄片，以及科幻片。

cues.en: So, the idea, is that our research participants will watch a movie from one of these four genres, and then afterwards they will give a happiness rating.
cues.zh: 研究參與者要看這四種類型中的一部電影，之後評分自己的快樂程度。

cues.en: So they'll rate from one to a hundred, how happy do you feel?
cues.zh: 以 1 到 100 分表示，現在有多快樂？

cues.en: Where a hundred means like super duper amazingly happy, and one is really, really sad, really horrible.
cues.zh: 100 表示超級無敵快樂，1 則是非常非常難過、糟透了。

cues.en: Okay, and that is our dependent variable.
cues.zh: 這就是依變數。

cues.en: Here we have the table of the factor and the different levels and the Ns per group, so the number of individuals per group.
cues.zh: 這張表列出因子、各水準，以及各組的 N，也就是各組人數。

cues.en: Now that's a rather small number, but that's because, well I don't really have a good reason for this.
cues.zh: 人數相當少，原因是——其實我沒有很好的理由。

cues.en: I guess the reason is that with a small sample size, I can show you every single data point.
cues.zh: 大概是因為樣本小，就能展示每個資料點。

cues.en: Now, notice also that we have an unbalanced design.
cues.zh: 也請注意，這是不平衡設計。

cues.en: This is an unbalanced ANOVA, because the different cells have different numbers of data points.
cues.zh: 是不平衡 ANOVA，因為各格的資料點數不同。

cues.en: So five, five, and only four people watched the documentary.
cues.zh: 這裡 5 人、這裡 5 人，紀錄片則只有 4 人。

cues.en: I don't know, maybe the documentary was so boring that one person just dropped out in the middle of the experiment, she refused to participate.
cues.zh: 也許紀錄片太無聊，有個人在實驗中途退出，她拒絕繼續參與。

cues.en: Anyway.
cues.zh: 總之。

cues.en: Okay, so here we have the data.
cues.zh: 這裡是資料。

cues.en: This is made up data of course, I made up all these numbers.
cues.zh: 當然是編造的，所有數字都是我編的。

cues.en: So we can see that there's one data point missing here, and it's interesting to just sort of look through the rest of the data.
cues.zh: 這裡少了一個資料點，也可以稍微看看其他資料。

cues.en: As I've mentioned many times before, it's always really important to visualize your data.
cues.zh: 之前多次提過，把資料視覺化總是非常重要。

cues.en: And when you have a really small data set like this, you can literally just look at the numbers, you can print out all the numbers and just look at them.
cues.zh: 資料集很小時，可以直接看數字，把全部數字印出來檢視。

cues.en: Of course, that's not a very scalable method.
cues.zh: 當然，這種方法不太能擴充到大量資料。

cues.en: So, you want to have other data visualization tricks up your sleeve as well, which of course you do, by this point in the course.
cues.zh: 所以也要準備其他視覺化技巧，上課到現在，你當然已經有這些技巧。

cues.en: We'll also look at some bar plots later on.
cues.zh: 稍後也會看一些長條圖。

cues.en: Okay, so these are the raw data.
cues.zh: 這些是原始資料。

cues.en: So I ran these through an ANOVA, and this is the resulting ANOVA table.
cues.zh: 我對它們執行 ANOVA，這是得到的 ANOVA 表。

cues.en: So the raw data in the previous slide, I made up, I just made up those numbers, but these are really the real numbers from those data.
cues.zh: 上一張投影片的原始資料，是我隨意編出的數字，但這裡是真正從那些資料算出的數值。

cues.en: So this is the true ANOVA table and this should look familiar.
cues.zh: 這是真正的 ANOVA 表，看起來應該很熟悉。

cues.en: It's in fact, what I showed you a few slides ago.
cues.zh: 其實幾張投影片之前就展示過。

cues.en: Now I would like to talk about this ANOVA table a little bit more than what I did previously.
cues.zh: 現在想比先前更深入談這張表。

cues.en: So I told you in the, one of the first few videos here, in this section, that the total sum of squares
cues.zh: 本單元前幾支影片之一提過，總平方和

cues.en: is the total amount of variance in the entire dataset.
cues.zh: 是整份資料集的總變異。

cues.en: And, that the idea of an ANOVA is to break up the total variability into two groups, or two sort of partitions.
cues.zh: ANOVA 的概念，是把總變異拆成兩組，或兩個部分。

cues.en: One partition is the between groups variability.
cues.zh: 一部分是組間變異。

cues.en: This is the variance in the data that we can specifically attribute to our experimental manipulation, which of course in this case is the movie genre, the different types of movies.
cues.zh: 可以明確歸因於實驗操弄的資料變異，這裡當然是電影類型、不同種類的電影。

cues.en: And then there's the within group variance, and that is all of the variability that is across the different individuals within each bin,
cues.zh: 另一部分是組內變異，也就是每個區間，

cues.en: within each level, or in this case movie genre.
cues.zh: 每個水準，這裡也就是各電影類型內，不同個體之間的變異。

cues.en: And so if that's really true, we should find that this number plus this number equals this number.
cues.zh: 如果這是真的，這個數字加這個數字，就應該等於這個數字。

cues.en: So I would like you to pause the video, and just, you know, bust out a calculator, or do this by hand if you prefer, or in your head if you're really capable of doing that.
cues.zh: 希望你暫停影片，拿出計算機，或者喜歡手算也可以，夠厲害的話，甚至可以心算。

cues.en: And add up these two numbers and confirm that you got this number.
cues.zh: 把這兩個數字加起來，確認得到這個數字。

cues.en: Okay, how did it go?
cues.zh: 結果如何？

cues.en: Did it work out?
cues.zh: 成立嗎？

cues.en: Did these two numbers sum to this?
cues.zh: 兩個數字相加，等於這個嗎？

cues.en: The answer is yes.
cues.zh: 答案是對的。

cues.en: You might get a little bit of an error.
cues.zh: 可能會有一點誤差。

cues.en: I actually, I have to admit, I didn't double check this myself, but I truncated these values here so it's not actually 0.42, there's a couple of numbers here.
cues.zh: 得承認，我自己沒有再確認，但我截短了這些數字，所以不是真的只到 0.42，後面還有幾位。

cues.en: So it is possible that these two do not add up exactly to this, at this level of precision, but I'm sure you got it to be very close.
cues.zh: 因此，這個精度下，兩者可能不精確等於這個值，但相信結果非常接近。

cues.en: Okay, and we can review this information here.
cues.zh: 再回顧這裡的資訊。

cues.en: I've already gone through this, but we can look at the degrees of freedom column here, and infer the number of total participants, which is 19,
cues.zh: 之前說明過，查看自由度這一欄，可以推得總參與者人數為 19，

cues.en: and the total number of levels within our factor, which is four.
cues.zh: 因子中的水準總數是 4。

cues.en: And then we have our mean squared error, and that is just the sum of squares divided by the degrees of freedom.
cues.zh: 接著是均方誤差，就是平方和除以自由度。

cues.en: So, pretty straightforward here.
cues.zh: 相當直接。

cues.en: This number literally comes from this number divided by this number.
cues.zh: 這個數字就是這個除以這個。

cues.en: Now, we're not showing the mean square total here.
cues.zh: 這裡沒有顯示總均方。

cues.en: And you might wonder why that is the case.
cues.zh: 你可能想知道原因。

cues.en: It would be pretty easy to compute.
cues.zh: 它其實很容易計算。

cues.en: And the main reason is that we don't actually need it for the F statistic.
cues.zh: 主要原因是，F 統計量不需要它。

cues.en: The F statistic is not based on the total variance, it's based on the ratio of the between group variants and the within group variants.
cues.zh: F 統計量不是根據總變異，而是根據組間與組內變異的比值。

cues.en: But, here's another thing I would like you to pause the video and work through.
cues.zh: 這裡還有一個希望你暫停影片思考的問題。

cues.en: First you're gonna do some thinking and then you're gonna have to do a little bit of calculation.
cues.zh: 先思考，再做一點計算。

cues.en: So, the thinking part, is about the sum of these two numbers.
cues.zh: 思考的是，這兩個數字的總和。

cues.en: So we've already established that the sum of these two numbers is the total variance in the signal, in the dataset, and that equals the total sum of squares here.
cues.zh: 我們已經確定，這兩個數字的總和，是訊號、資料集的總變異，等於這裡的總平方和。

cues.en: Now the question is, are the two, would you expect these two numbers to sum to produce this number, which I'm actually not showing here.
cues.zh: 問題是，你預期這兩個數字相加，會得到這個我沒有顯示出來的數字嗎？

cues.en: So does the sum of the mean squares, for between groups and within groups, equal the mean square for the total?
cues.zh: 也就是，組間均方加上組內均方，是否等於總均方？

cues.en: So that's, so yeah, pause the video first, think about your answer, and then you actually have to compute this number and then add these two and see what you get.
cues.zh: 先暫停、想想答案，再算出這個數字，把這兩個相加，看看結果。

cues.en: Okay, how did it go?
cues.zh: 結果如何？

cues.en: Did you pause the video and think about it?
cues.zh: 有暫停並想一想嗎？

cues.en: So it's a little bit tricky.
cues.zh: 這有點難。

cues.en: So first of all, the answer is no.
cues.zh: 首先，答案是否。

cues.en: And you can confirm that empirically, because this divided by 18 is gonna be, I don't know exactly, but somewhere between 100 and 200,
cues.zh: 可以實際計算確認，這個除以 18，大概會落在 100 到 200 之間，確切我不知道，

cues.en: and these two numbers summed together is less than 700, but certainly you know, around 660 or whatever it is.
cues.zh: 這兩個相加則小於 700，但肯定在 660 左右，或類似的數字。

cues.en: So they're not even close.
cues.zh: 所以一點都不接近。

cues.en: Now is that surprising?
cues.zh: 這令人驚訝嗎？

cues.en: It actually shouldn't be so surprising.
cues.zh: 其實不應該太驚訝。

cues.en: And that's because of how we are dividing these numbers here.
cues.zh: 原因是這裡的除法方式。

cues.en: So here we are dividing by N minus one, and here we're dividing by factors of K.
cues.zh: 這裡除以 N 減 1，這裡則除以與 K 有關的因子。

cues.en: So as soon as we start averaging, we start computing the mean square, then we are beginning to weight the variances in different ways according to the number of sub partitions
cues.zh: 開始平均、計算均方後，就會依據各個主要變異部分中，

cues.en: of each major partition of the variance.
cues.zh: 子部分的數量，以不同方式替變異加權。

cues.en: Okay, and then we get the F score, and that's literally just this number divided by this number.
cues.zh: 接著得到 F 分數，就是這個數字除以這個數字。

cues.en: And you know, you can already see that it's gonna be a little bit higher than 10 because if the F value were 10, then this would be 460.
cues.zh: 已經可以看出會大於 10 一點，因為如果 F 是 10，這裡就會是 460。

cues.en: So, and if you like, you could also, you know, divide this number by this number and confirm that you get 13.25.
cues.zh: 如果願意，可以把這個除以這個，確認得到 13.25。

cues.en: Okay, so that gives us our F statistic.
cues.zh: 這就得到 F 統計量。

cues.en: And so far all of this stuff you can actually compute by hand.
cues.zh: 目前所有這些，其實都可以手算。

cues.en: This isn't really hard to compute.
cues.zh: 不是真的很難。

cues.en: I mean this thing, you know, these will take you a little while to figure out.
cues.zh: 這些東西可能會讓你花一點時間。

cues.en: But for such a small dataset like this, this stuff isn't so hard to compute.
cues.zh: 但這麼小的資料集，計算並不太難。

cues.en: This gets a little trickier, to evaluate a F statistic according to a probability density function, by hand.
cues.zh: 比較棘手的是，用機率密度函數手動評估 F 統計量。

cues.en: So let me show you how that gets done by the computer.
cues.zh: 來示範電腦如何完成。

cues.en: So here we have a null hypothesis distribution of F statistics.
cues.zh: 這是虛無假設下的 F 統計量分布。

cues.en: So, this is the probability density of F values expected under the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 也就是虛無假設下，預期 F 值的機率密度。

cues.en: Now, the exact shape of this blue distribution here depends on our degrees of freedom.
cues.zh: 這個藍色分布的確切形狀，取決於自由度。

cues.en: And you had the opportunity, quite a while ago in this course, that must have been in the section on descriptive statistics in the video, the coding video,
cues.zh: 課程很早之前，應該是在描述統計單元，一支程式影片，

cues.en: called Data from Different Distributions.
cues.zh: 叫作「不同分布的資料」，曾經有機會

cues.en: So you had the opportunity before, to explore how this F distribution changes, the shape of this distribution changes, as a function of the these two numbers,
cues.zh: 探索這個 F 分布的形狀，如何隨這兩個數字改變，

cues.en: which you now know are the numerator and denominator degrees of freedom.
cues.zh: 現在你知道，它們是分子與分母自由度。

cues.en: So if you like, after this video, you could go back, find the code from that previous video and play around with this a little bit more.
cues.zh: 如果願意，影片結束後可以回頭找那支影片的程式碼，再稍微玩一下。

cues.en: But that's okay, so the idea is that this is our null hypothesis probability distribution.
cues.zh: 總之，這是虛無假設的機率分布。

cues.en: This orange line here actually corresponds to the alpha level of 0.05.
cues.zh: 橘線對應 alpha 水準 0.05。

cues.en: So a P-value of 0.05, for these two degrees of freedom, corresponds to an F value of whatever this number is,
cues.zh: 對這兩個自由度而言，P 值 0.05 對應的 F 值，是這個數字，

cues.en: I guess around 3.5, maybe 3.2.
cues.zh: 我猜大約 3.5，也許 3.2。

cues.en: So this would be called like the critical value of F.
cues.zh: 這就稱為 F 的臨界值。

cues.en: And you can see our observed F statistic is way beyond that critical value.
cues.zh: 可以看到，觀察到的 F 統計量遠超過臨界值。

cues.en: And so it turns out that if you evaluate this on the probability distribution, the probability of getting a F statistic of 13.15, or larger,
cues.zh: 在機率分布上評估，得到 F 統計量為 13.15 或更大的機率，

cues.en: Or actually it was 0.0002.
So it's even smaller than what I said, and I think I said 13.15, but you don't, you get the idea.
cues.zh: 比剛才說的更小，而且我好像說成 13.15，不過你了解意思。

cues.en: Okay, so, the conclusion, is that the mean of at least one level is statistically significantly different from the mean of at least one other level.
cues.zh: 結論是，至少一個水準的平均值，與至少另一個水準平均值的差異達到統計顯著。

cues.en: So, that's sort of the like nerdy stats speak way of interpreting this P-value in this ANOVA table.
cues.zh: 這就是用比較學術的統計術語，解讀這張 ANOVA 表的 P 值。

cues.en: And what this really means is that people were happier after at least one genre compared to at least one other genre.
cues.zh: 真正意思是，看完至少一種電影類型之後，人們比看完至少另一種類型更快樂。

cues.en: So, like, as I've discussed in previous videos here, this conclusion is a little bit vague.
cues.zh: 如前幾支影片所說，這個結論有一點模糊。

cues.en: It doesn't tell us which movies make people happy, it just says that somehow the movie genre is affecting people's happiness.
cues.zh: 不會告訴我們哪些電影讓人快樂，只說電影類型以某種方式影響快樂。

cues.en: Okay, so to do this, we need to visualize the data, and that's what I'm showing here.
cues.zh: 因此需要把資料視覺化，這裡就是如此。

cues.en: This is actually a graph that I showed previously.
cues.zh: 這張圖之前展示過。

cues.en: So, now we have the labels mapped on, these are horror movies, romantic comedies, documentaries, and sci-fis.
cues.zh: 現在有標籤，分別是恐怖片、浪漫喜劇、紀錄片與科幻片。

cues.en: And here are the average happiness ratings.
cues.zh: 這裡是平均快樂評分。

cues.en: So, notice I'm not showing any error bars here, so those could be added, we could show some standard deviation bars within each group, but that's not what I did here.
cues.zh: 注意，沒有畫誤差棒，可以加上各組的標準差誤差棒，但這裡沒有。

cues.en: Okay, so this kind of helps us a little bit, but we still need to get in further detail.
cues.zh: 這稍微有幫助，但還需要更多細節。

cues.en: We still need to run the actual post hoc comparison tests to know which groups are significantly different from which other groups.
cues.zh: 仍必須真正進行事後比較檢定，才知道哪些組與哪些其他組有顯著差異。

cues.en: So this is a problem.
cues.zh: 這就是問題。

cues.en: This, you know, this looks like a pretty small difference here, but you know, if we had a really large sample size, and very small variability, in theory, these two could be significantly different
cues.zh: 這裡看起來差異很小，但如果樣本非常大，變異非常小，理論上這兩組可能有

cues.en: from each other.
cues.zh: 顯著差異。

cues.en: That's possible given this graph.
cues.zh: 從這張圖看，是有可能的。

cues.en: So we need to do some formal testing.
cues.zh: 所以需要正式檢定。

cues.en: We can't just rely on our visual inspection without any supporting statistical inference methods.
cues.zh: 不能只憑目視檢查，而沒有統計推論方法支持。

cues.en: Okay, so, what I did was apply the two key post hoc comparison test, and I decided to test all possible pairs in here, which is a total of six possible pairs.
cues.zh: 因此我使用 Tukey 事後比較檢定，決定測試所有可能配對，總共六對。

cues.en: So I compared horror against, so the happiness ratings for horror against rom-com, horror against documentaries, and so on, all these possible pairs.
cues.zh: 比較恐怖片與——也就是恐怖片與浪漫喜劇的快樂評分、恐怖片與紀錄片，以及所有其他可能配對。

cues.en: And then it turned out that these were the results.
cues.zh: 最後得到這些結果。

cues.en: So, what I'm showing here, this is a common way to show statistically significant differences between groups in a multiple comparisons test
cues.zh: 這是呈現 ANOVA 結果中，多重比較檢定的組間統計顯著差異，

cues.en: in an ANOVA result.
cues.zh: 很常見的一種方式。

cues.en: So the lines tell you which two conditions were different from each other.
cues.zh: 線條表示哪兩個條件彼此不同。

cues.en: So the fact that there's a line going from this group to this group tells you that people were significantly happier after watching sci-fi compared to after watching
cues.zh: 從這一組連到這一組的線，表示看完科幻片，比看完

cues.en: horror.
cues.zh: 恐怖片之後顯著更快樂。

cues.en: No big shocker there.
cues.zh: 這並不令人驚訝。

cues.en: And this is also significant.
cues.zh: 這裡也顯著。

cues.en: So, people are happier after watching documentaries than after horror movies.
cues.zh: 看完紀錄片，比看完恐怖片更快樂。

cues.en: These two groups don't differ.
cues.zh: 這兩組沒有差異。

cues.en: So you can see there's no yellow line that is going, that is connecting these two bars.
cues.zh: 所以沒有黃色線條連接這兩個長條。

cues.en: So people were equally miserable after watching horror movies and romantic comedies.
cues.zh: 人們看完恐怖片與浪漫喜劇，同樣不快樂。

cues.en: Likewise, these two bars are different from each other and romcoms and sci-fis are also different from each other.
cues.zh: 同樣，這兩個長條彼此不同，浪漫喜劇與科幻片也彼此不同。

cues.en: And these two bars are actually not different from each other.
cues.zh: 而這兩個長條實際上沒有差異。

cues.en: By the way, in case you are curious about my own personal movie taste, I would be, I enjoy horror movies and I enjoy sci-fi movies.
cues.zh: 如果你好奇我的電影喜好，我喜歡恐怖片，也喜歡科幻片。

cues.en: And my happiness rating after watching a romcom is gonna be right, I don't know.
cues.zh: 看完浪漫喜劇之後，我的快樂評分大概會在——我也不知道。

cues.en: Are we allowed to have negative numbers for happiness in here?
cues.zh: 這裡的快樂程度可以用負數嗎？

cues.en: Anyway.
cues.zh: 總之。

cues.en: So in this video I gave you another example of a one-way ANOVA, and now in the next video you'll get to see how to implement these kinds of statistical procedures
cues.zh: 這支影片又舉了一個單因子 ANOVA 的例子，下一支影片會看到如何把這些統計程序

cues.en: in code.
cues.zh: 實作成程式碼。
